title: Self-hosting guide
intro: Run the complete GlassFolio app on your own computer or server with Docker. Your encrypted vault is written to a volume you control, nothing depends on our infrastructure, and the source code is public.

quickstart.title: Quick start
quickstart.body: Clone the repository and start the container. The npm script checks your network settings first, then builds the image and starts it in the background.
quickstart.open: Open {{url}} in your browser and create your vault. The first build takes a few minutes; later starts take seconds.
quickstart.stop: Stop the app (your data stays in the volume)

items.docker: Docker Engine 24 or later with Compose v2, or Docker Desktop on macOS and Windows (WSL 2).
items.node: Node.js 22, used by the start script to check your network settings before Docker starts.
items.git: Git, to download the code and later pull updates.
items.resources: About 1 GB of disk space for the image. The container is capped at 512 MB of memory.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.body: Settings are environment variables. Put the stable ones in docker/docker.env, or prefix the start command with them for a one-off change. Keep the access token out of files: set it in your shell.

vars.GLASSFOLIO_PORT: Port on your machine where the app answers.
vars.GLASSFOLIO_BIND: Network address the port listens on. 127.0.0.1 keeps the app private to this computer.
vars.GLASSFOLIO_DATA: Where your encrypted data is stored: the named Docker volume, or a host folder writable by user ID 1000.
vars.GLASSFOLIO_ACCESS_TOKEN: Password required by the browser when the app is reachable from the network. At least 16 characters.
vars.GLASSFOLIO_ALLOWED_HOSTS: Comma-separated domain names allowed to use the vault API, for example behind a reverse proxy. localhost and IP addresses always work.
vars.GLASSFOLIO_CSP_CONNECT_SRC: Extra origins the page may call, space-separated, such as a remote Ollama server.

network.title: Access from your network
network.body: By default only this computer can open the app. To reach it from a phone or another machine, bind it to every interface and set an access token; the start script refuses to expose the app without one.
network.login: Your browser then asks for a user name and password: the user name is glassfolio and the password is the token. The /health endpoint stays open for monitoring.
network.proxy: For access from outside your home network, put the app behind a reverse proxy with HTTPS and list its domain in GLASSFOLIO_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Never expose port 3000 directly to the internet.

backup.title: Back up and restore
backup.body: Everything you enter is in the container's /data volume, already encrypted. This command writes a compressed copy to the current folder while the app keeps running.
backup.restore: To restore a backup, stop the container, replace the volume's content with the archive, then start it again.

update.title: Update
update.body: Pull the latest code and run the start script again. The image is rebuilt and your data volume is kept as it is.

ai.title: Local AI with Ollama
ai.body: The assistant can run entirely on your machine with Ollama, so no portfolio data leaves your network. Install Ollama, pull a model, then start it so that it accepts requests from the app's address.
ai.settings: In GlassFolio, open Settings, choose Ollama as the AI provider and keep the default address http://localhost:11434.
ai.remote: If Ollama runs on another machine, add its address to GLASSFOLIO_CSP_CONNECT_SRC so the page is allowed to call it.
